title: Mendha Lekha: our village, our rule
body: Mendha Lekha is a small tribal village in the Gadchiroli district of Maharashtra, inhabited mainly by the Gond tribe. It became the first village in India to gain rights over its forest resources under the Forest Rights Act, 2006. The villagers follow the principle of Mawa Nate Mawa Raj, which means 'our village, our rule', so that all decisions are taken collectively through the Gram Sabha. They protect and sustainably use about 1,800 hectares of forest by regulating tree cutting, preventing forest fires and promoting bamboo harvesting as a renewable resource. The revenue from forest produce is spent on community welfare such as education and infrastructure. The model shows how traditional knowledge, rights, duties and democratic participation can work together for sustainable forest conservation.
